producer_report.summary: Added `check_outcome_state` to reading acceptance in `crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs`. Root cause: reading acceptance turned a delivery verb (publish, deploy, share, release) into a narrow deliverable, with no check against the state the user observes. Jobs 20261014-082328-g6vy, 20261014-174815-7bf8 and 20261017-173508-0wtc were read that way. The check is one `step!` line in `refusing_check`, after `check_governance_coverage`, so governance refusals keep precedence. It applies when the reading has a capability, no question and a deliverable. It looks for a delivery verb that starts a sentence, line or bullet in the request or, for a retry, in the earlier request. A leading `-`, `*`, `•`, `1.`, `1)` or `(a)`, and `please`, `then` or `now`, are skipped. A following word such as `of` or `notes`, and a verb inside a list, mean it is not an instruction. It then needs a criterion of any kind that names an observable state (url, reachable, served, live at, downloadable, installable, tag, published release, visible to, `http://`, `https://`), or an `out_of_scope` item that names the verb. Otherwise it refuses, and the error lists the words to add and the out_of_scope exit. The reader prompt and `READING_RULES` are unchanged. I updated four existing tests and one corpus case that used a publish or deploy request with file-only criteria; each now has a criterion naming a reachable URL. I added unit tests, 12 corpus cases, three corpus input forms, a CHANGELOG entry and decision D161. The 5% refusal share is an estimate that I did not measure. The replay of past readings runs at verification.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. A new unit test in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs shows check_outcome_state refusing a reading for the request 'Publish a first explainer page on how firstmate handles work.' whose criteria only say a file exists. The error names the missing observable state, such as the URL or reachability. The test fails when the check is removed.
criteria_check.evidence: `check_outcome_state_refuses_a_publish_request_whose_criteria_only_say_a_file_exists` asserts the error contains 'publish', 'URL', 'reachable' and 'out_of_scope', and that `refusing_check` names `check_outcome_state`. `cargo test -p athena-core -q` passed (1080 lib tests). Without the step! line `refusing_check` would return None and the test would fail; I did not run that removal.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core`. A unit test shows the same request accepted when a criterion names a reachable URL or served state. Further cases cover deploy, share and release, and show no refusal when the request has no delivery verb, for example 'Add a timeout setting'.
criteria_check.evidence: `check_outcome_state_accepts_a_reading_that_names_the_state` covers reachable/served/live at/http. `check_outcome_state_covers_deploy_share_and_release` refuses file-only and accepts with a state, and covers the out_of_scope exit. `check_outcome_state_leaves_other_requests_alone` covers 'Add a timeout setting', noun uses, mid-sentence use, decline, question and no deliverables, and the retry request. All pass in `cargo test -p athena-core -q`.

criteria_check.criterion: Grep crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs shows a `step!(check_outcome_state(` line inside refusing_check, with a doc comment that names the root cause (a delivery verb read as a narrow deliverable, with no check against the state the user observes) and cites jobs 20261014-082328-g6vy, 20261014-174815-7bf8 and 20261017-173508-0wtc.
criteria_check.evidence: The step! line is in refusing_check after check_governance_coverage. The one-paragraph doc on `pub fn check_outcome_state` holds the cause text and the three job ids. `check_outcome_state_doc_names_the_root_cause` asserts both and passes.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`. The corpus has a case in which check_outcome_state refuses and a matching accepting case. The corpus test still passes, including its rule that every step! has a refusing case.
criteria_check.evidence: `publish-reading-names-no-observable-state` refuses by check_outcome_state; `publish-reading-names-a-reachable-url` accepts. The dash, star, numbered and lettered bullet cases, the retry pair, and the mid-sentence and noun cases were added. The refusal_corpus binary passed within `cargo test -p athena-core -q`.

criteria_check.criterion: The change refuses more readings. Expected 5% of newly refused readings. A replay of past readings is expected to hold the job only above 10%. The higher refusal rate is intended: the check applies only to requests with a delivery verb whose reading names no observable state.
criteria_check.evidence: The doc comment and the CHANGELOG entry say 'the higher refusal rate is intended' and 'expected 5% of newly refused readings'. `check_outcome_state_refusal_is_declared_intended` asserts replay_declaration reads 5 and both texts contain them; it passes. The 5% is an estimate; the replay was not run here.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`. All three pass, including the briefs.rs test that asserts READING_RULES has 6 entries.

open_issues: Decision for the user: a verb in the middle of a sentence ('Build the docs and publish them') is not checked, to keep false refusals low. D161 states this.
The 5% newly-refused share is an estimate. If the replay of past readings measures above 10%, narrow the verb scan or the not-a-delivery word list.
A negated criterion ('not reachable') and a retry whose earlier request is not in the attempt record are not detected. D161 states both.
mistakes: The first draft of the doc comment had a blank `///` line, so the doc test failed. I merged it into one paragraph.
The first D161 draft cited D147 and D153 for things they do not cover. I checked their headings and corrected the text before reporting.
learnings: The tool-result file for a large cargo test run sits outside the working directory, so Grep and Read refuse it. Use `cargo test -q` to keep output short.
The doc-comment source tests need a one-paragraph doc with no blank `///` line, directly after a blank line, and the first occurrence of `pub fn name(` in the file is the real one.
`normalised()` and `has_phrase()` in reading.rs are the shared helpers for whole-word, lowercase matching.
docs/decisions.md is over 256KB; append with an Edit anchored on the last entry's final lines.
D147 is about repo paths and D153 about boundary words; neither is the governance check, which has no entry of its own. D148 is the refusal corpus.
desires: Read access to the saved tool-result file of a long test run, or a way to filter test output without piping.
